result.rationale: The diff shows refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response when sync mode is active ('const response = await fetch(...); return response;'), while zoho-bigin's CalendarService wraps it and then reads 'tokenInfo.data.error' on the returned value. A fetch Response object has no '.data' property, so in credential-sharing mode this throws TypeError. Also note zoho-bigin passes 'credentialId' (likely a number/string credential id) as userId, compounding the issue. The mechanism is verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but this axios-based code reads `tokenInfo.data.error`; fetch Responses have no `.data` property, so the line throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'error'). Zoho Bigin token refresh crashes on every invocation in credential-sharing deployments, breaking Bigin calendar sync entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set and the third argument is truthy, the function returns a native `fetch(...)` `Response` object (not an axios response). In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenInfo` is assigned from `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then the code does `if (!tokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data` property, so in sync mode this will throw at runtime (attempting to read `error` of `undefined`).
